sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Orionid meteor shower has become active as Earth travels through a trail of dust and debris shed by Halley's Comet. Tiny particles enter the atmosphere at around 41 miles per second, creating glowing trails that can briefly linger in the night sky.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The shower peaks overnight from 21 to 22 October, offering up to 20 meteors per hour in dark areas. Rain across the UK is expected to move away early during the peak night, but wetter and windier weather may follow later in the week. Activity continues until 7 November, though light from the approaching full Moon on 26 October may obscure fainter meteors.

gist: Tony Hall has lived in the UK for 50 years after arriving from Barbados.
Despite serving his sentence, he remains destitute and unable to work or access normal services.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Tony Hall arrived in the UK from Barbados in 1976 at age 12. In 2001, he was convicted of conspiracy to rob and having a firearm with intent, serving eight years in prison. Following his release, the Home Office placed him on a deportation list. For 14 years, he has faced fortnightly reporting requirements, preventing him from working, renting, or rebuilding his life.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The case highlights ongoing issues from the Windrush scandal, where people with long-term UK ties face deportation and administrative limbo. Critics point to the unfairness of prolonged uncertainty and double jeopardy after individuals have served their criminal sentences.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Hall's solicitor has called on the Home Office to reconsider the case, arguing the deportation order was issued in error given Hall's background as a British Citizen of the UK and Colonies.

fivew: The Home Office is trying to deport Tony Hall, who has lived in the UK for 50 years.
Over a period of 14 years following his release from prison.
Because of a past criminal conviction, despite his long-term residence and Windrush-era links.

quotes.text: Compassion is not exactly their middle name
Whatever the legal complexities of an individual case, people should not be left in prolonged uncertainty about their future.

India-born US-raised actor Sunil Malhotra took over the role, replacing Hank Azaria. Azaria previously stepped down following a 2017 documentary by Hari Kondabolu that highlighted racial stereotypes in the character's portrayal. Apu's wife Manjula also received a new voice actor, Janina Gavankar.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The return marks a significant shift for the long-running US animation series after years of controversy over racial representations. Malhotra collaborated with showrunners to ensure the character's comeback was culturally appropriate and acknowledged past mistakes, describing the process as a reclamation.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Showrunner Matt Selman stated that Apu and the Nahasapeemapetilon family will appear on the programme more frequently in future episodes.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: BBC Panorama found private firms exploit supported exempt accommodation, receiving housing benefits without providing required care to vulnerable residents. Providers use social media offers to attract tenants, while some claim payments for non-existent ghost tenants. Residents reported inadequate support and substandard conditions, though accused providers disputed claims of neglect.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: In Birmingham alone, the DWP spent £410m on supported housing last financial year. Non-profit providers transfer public funds to private management firms making vast profits. Five of the city's six largest providers failed regulatory standards, prompting accusations of wasted public funds and benefit fraud.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The Regulator of Social Housing has launched action to close Concept Housing Association over serious operational failings. Meanwhile, Birmingham City Council stated officers are working to eliminate fraud and substandard accommodation.

gist: NHS leaders warn up to 20 smaller maternity units in England may face closure.
Staff shortages and rising caesarean births threaten patient safety at smaller hospital units.
The Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists opposes closures, advocating increased staff investment.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: NHS managers have warned that up to 20 smaller consultant-led maternity units across England may need to shut. While the Health Service Journal previously estimated 24 units were at risk, NHS Alliance acute lead Matthew Hopkins cited 20. The organisation stated that staffing shortages and a sharp increase in caesarean births leave smaller units unable to safely maintain round-the-clock care.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Health bosses argue consolidating services will improve safety and care quality for mothers and babies. However, closures would particularly impact rural and coastal communities, forcing women to travel much further to give birth. The Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists called for alternative solutions, urging ministers to resolve pressures through workforce expansion and training rather than closures.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: A government taskforce on maternity and neonatal care will release recommendations before Christmas, which will form a national action plan announced by Health Secretary Yvette Cooper. Meanwhile, in Devon, services at Barnstaple remain suspended ahead of an October readiness assessment.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The World Food Programme has cut food aid to Gaza, reducing monthly recipients from 1.6 million to 1.1 million. Daily community kitchen meals have fallen from 250,000 to 150,000, while ration boxes and cash transfers have also been reduced.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Over 80% of Gaza is unemployed, and two-thirds of the population relies on food aid. Most farmland is occupied and fishing is barred, leaving residents unable to feed themselves amid ongoing displacement and winter conditions.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The agency urgently seeks over £300m (the BBC reports $450m or £338m) to maintain critical operations over the next six months. Sourcing and shipping ration supplies could take about three months if funding arrives.

gist: Wildfires in northern boreal regions are accelerating permafrost thaw and releasing ancient carbon.
Scientists and agencies are studying fire suppression and cultural burning to protect frozen soil.
New satellite networks and mapping are being developed to detect and target high-risk blazes.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Intensifying wildfires across northern boreal forests have accelerated permafrost thaw, leading researchers and fire managers to test intervention strategies. In regions like Alaska, initiatives are trialling fire suppression and intentional burning to safeguard carbon-dense soils rather than solely defending human habitations and property.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Permafrost stores roughly twice as much carbon as the atmosphere. Intense blazes burn away the insulating organic topsoil, causing rapid thaw and releasing potent greenhouse gases. This threatens to create a feedback loop that transforms northern carbon sinks into major global emission sources.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Collaborators under the North Fire initiative plan to expand risk mapping across Alaska and Canada and test cultural burning near Fort Yukon. Meanwhile, the FireSat satellite constellation will expand into the 2030s to help detect blazes early.

gist: Independent MP Helen Haines was struck by a car in Wangaratta.
Experts and politicians have warned of rising threats against public figures in Australia.
Police arrested a man at the scene and launched an investigation.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Independent MP Helen Haines was severely injured after being struck by a car outside her office in Wangaratta. Police arrested a 43-year-old man at the scene and seized a knife, though they have not confirmed if she was hit deliberately. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described it as an apparent attack, and federal police are assisting with the investigation.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The incident comes amid rising concern over threats, violence, and vandalism targeting Australian politicians. Experts cite social polarisation, online environments, and growing grievances as drivers. There are fears this could threaten Australia's open political culture, where MPs frequently interact with the public.

fivew: Independent MP Helen Haines and a 43-year-old man.
Outside her office in the regional Victorian town of Wangaratta.
Police and state officers are investigating the incident, and no motive has been officially confirmed.

gist: Kenya has confirmed nine Ebola cases in its first ever outbreak.
Authorities have enhanced screening and tracing while ruling out travel bans.
Concerns remain regarding border lapses and protection for health workers.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Kenya confirmed its first ever Ebola outbreak with nine cases, all linked to an initial patient who travelled from DR Congo and died. Four relatives, three health workers, and a hospital cleaner tested positive.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: As a regional transport hub, Kenya faces a steady risk of new cases. The doctors' union warned of understaffed border facilities and lapses, while the US issued a travel advisory.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Kenya remains open with no travel restrictions. The government has isolated most contacts, trained thousands of health workers, and enhanced border screening.

gist: Hackers breached an older system of open source AI coding agent OpenCode.
The attack affected 1.4% of users of the online platform OpenCode Console.
Attackers ran up unauthorized charges on users' connected AI accounts.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Attackers breached an older system of OpenCode overnight, affecting 1.4% of OpenCode Console users. Developers reported unauthorized charges and spending alerts on their AI accounts. While OpenCode described it as a distillation attack, skeptics called that framing an overstretch and argued it was a straightforward breach.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The incident highlighted difficulties in defending against large-scale cyberattacks when AI model safety guardrails refuse to analyse malicious payloads needed for defence work. Anthropic, Google and OpenAI blocked or worked to restore exposed keys, while refunds for unauthorised charges are underway.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: OpenCode stated that the incident remains ongoing. The company has instructed affected users to revoke and replace their API keys directly with each provider.

fivew: Hackers broke into an older system and ran up charges on users' AI accounts.
Attackers carried out a large-scale attack while OpenCode faced ongoing security pressures.

quotes.text: We had a security breach last night related to a large-scale distillation attack that impacted 1.4% of OpenCode Console users
Note this is the OpenCode Console, not OpenCode itself, those keys never come to us

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A researcher published an exploit chain as part of a proof-of-concept attack after submitting a bug report to Plex. The complex code uses unauthenticated SSRF, loopback pivot, security token theft, payload delivery, and execution. The bug finder reported using AI heavily to develop the exploit chain through iterative work and judgment calls.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Anyone using Plex should ensure the software is running version 1.43.3. Users can configure updates automatically or download and install them manually. Given active exploitation, outdated versions need immediate updates alongside properly securing media servers by restricting access or routing traffic through a reverse proxy.

sections.text: Amazon Web Services released a tool called TorchNeuron on Monday, allowing AI startups to easily move apps onto Amazon's Trainium chip by changing one line of configuration. The tool works with PyTorch and challenges Nvidia's dominant software advantage.

sections.text: Nvidia's CUDA software has made its hardware the default choice for AI. TorchNeuron aims to remove this lock-in, giving developers a way to use Amazon's cloud and custom chips while potentially lowering costs.

The taboo around gynaecological health contributes to diagnostic delays and shame.
Clare Baumhaeur developed vulval cancer after decades of undiagnosed lichen sclerosus.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Women suffered from intimate itching, soreness, and blisters that were repeatedly dismissed as thrush, herpes, or other conditions. Monica Thomas and Clare Baumhaeur faced long delays, misdiagnoses, and physical pain before receiving a biopsy and a diagnosis of lichen sclerosus. Clare also developed vulval cancer.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Social taboo and embarrassment prevent people from speaking about gynaecological symptoms. A lack of awareness among healthcare professionals leads to delayed diagnoses, affecting mental health and, in some cases, leading to severe complications like cancer.

sections.text: King Mohammed VI appointed Fatima Zahra El Mansouri as Morocco's first female prime minister. Her party, the Authenticity and Modernity Party, won the most seats in September's election and formed a four-party coalition holding 207 parliamentary seats.

sections.text: The appointment breaks a gender barrier, but has resurfaced conservative opposition and debate over women in leadership. sections.text: Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust faces three charges concerning the deaths of two young children who had sepsis. sections.text: A £17m extension to the design museum in Ghent, Belgium, has been built by Carmody Groarke with local firms Atama and Re-st. gist: UK job vacancies dropped by 21,000 to 691,000, reaching a five-year low.
Smaller businesses cut hiring because of increased labour expenses and elevated energy bills.
The unemployment rate fell to 4.7%, though youth joblessness remains a concern.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: UK job openings fell by 21,000 to 691,000 during the three months to September, marking the lowest figure in more than five years. The steepest decline occurred within construction. Over the three months to August, the overall unemployment rate fell to 4.7%, while real earnings grew by 0.8%.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Smaller firms are curbing recruitment because of climbing staffing overheads, including statutory wage increases and National Insurance changes, alongside higher energy bills. Although ministers cited employment resilience, youth unemployment reached 15.6%, leaving nearly one million young individuals outside work, education, or training.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Chancellor John Healey presents his first Budget next week, whilst analysts expect hiring to stay subdued due to persistent energy costs.

gist: Covid inquiry report criticises government protection of care homes during the pandemic.
Failings included lack of PPE, moving untested hospital patients, and tough visiting restrictions.
Systemic weaknesses and blanket do not resuscitate orders caused severe harm.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Covid inquiry sixth report found that government action to protect care homes came too late, resulting in over 43,000 recorded deaths. The care sector was an afterthought, suffering from personal protective equipment shortages, unsafe hospital discharges without sufficient testing, and strict visiting restrictions that went too far. Additionally, GPs imposed unlawful blanket do not resuscitate orders.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Long-standing sector weaknesses, such as high staff vacancies, zero-hours contracts, and fragmented services, undermined the pandemic response. This exposed residents to severe health declines, caused deep distress among care staff, and strained mental health.

sections.text: Unlike standard vision-language-action models, Eka relies on a vision-force-action model and reinforcement learning via physics simulation. sections.heading: What happens next

gist: Nini Rodgers was a historian of Ireland’s involvement with slavery and abolition.
She published Ireland, Slavery and Anti-Slavery: 1612-1865 in 2007 after a four-decade career.
She was a dedicated lecturer at Queen’s University Belfast and a campaigner for change.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Historian Nini Rodgers died at the age of 86. Throughout a four-decade career at Queen’s University Belfast, she taught thousands of students and championed part-time night degrees. In 2007, she published her major work, Ireland, Slavery and Anti-Slavery: 1612-1865, challenging Ireland's self-image regarding the transatlantic slave trade. She was the daughter of Marie and the poet WR Rodgers, and partner to the late historian Jack Gray.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Rodgers's research meticulously unmasked the reality of Ireland's involvement in slavery, replacing comforting fables with precise knowledge. She also shaped generations of historians and brought higher education to new kinds of people through her commitment to part-time students.

sections.text: Counter-terrorism police re-arrested two men on suspicion of assisting Iranian intelligence under the National Security Act 2023. sections.text: Engineers at MIT and EPFL created a lightweight flapping-wing aerial-aquatic vehicle weighing under 300 grams. sections.text: Moving through both air and water is difficult because water is much denser than air. This robot overcomes this challenge without needing feet. It could provide a cheaper way for oceanographers and marine biologists to sample hazardous aquatic areas.

gist: New research shows that one bad apple can spoil the barrel.
Observing flagrant rule-breaking by others leads people to greatly increase violations.
People are more influenced by others who share their political leanings.

sections.text: Researchers recruited 750 people in the US for an online experiment involving monetary rewards and rule-breaking choices. Participants were shown whether others followed the rules, the extent of violations, and political affiliations.

Police treated the incident as a suspected antisemitic hate crime.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Three Jewish women reported being attacked in north-east London. Members of a Jewish neighbourhood watch group detained a suspect before police arrived and made an arrest.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Police treated the event as a suspected antisemitic hate crime, prompting heightened patrols and discussions with local community leaders to offer reassurance.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The suspect remains in custody following further arrest for a separate incident, while police appeal for witnesses and additional victims.

gist: Sarina Wiegman has agreed a two-year contract extension as England manager until Euro 2029.

England next face a two-legged play-off tie against Ukraine to qualify for the World Cup.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Sarina Wiegman has committed her future as England manager by signing a two-year extension until Euro 2029. Her prior arrangement was scheduled to conclude following next summer's World Cup.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Wiegman has led the Lionesses to two consecutive European Championship titles and reached five major finals in a row. The deal prevents speculation about her future, giving the team stability. FA chief Mark Bullingham commended her tournament achievements and leadership.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: England will face Ukraine across two legs in round two of the World Cup play-offs, seeking to seal qualification for the tournament in Brazil.

fivew: Sarina Wiegman signed a two-year contract extension to remain England manager until Euro 2029.
She wants to continue working with the squad and help them realise their potential.

gist: Ronald Araujo joined Liverpool on a season-long loan from Barcelona.
Injuries to defenders created an opportunity for Araujo to shine.
Liverpool have an option to buy him for forty-seven million pounds.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Ronald Araujo joined Liverpool on a season-long loan from Barcelona as a stopgap solution. He has started eight of ten games under Andoni Iraola, playing at right-back and centre-back, and scored his first goal against LASK.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Liverpool faced an injury crisis with Conor Bradley and Jeremie Frimpong sidelined. Araujo seized his chance, showcasing his versatility and experience while helping solve the team's defensive problems.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Araujo is focused on playing and enjoying every day. Liverpool have an option to buy him for forty-seven million pounds in the summer, though it remains to be seen what the future holds.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Athletes like Jake Smith and Brian Smith suffered severe injuries and health issues due to under-fuelling and REDs, driven by the sports culture of being as light as possible.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: REDs causes hormonal disruption, bone stress injuries, and long-term health problems. While women have menstrual cycles as a warning sign, men suffer more subtle symptoms and face stigma.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Experts and organisations are pushing for better education, nutrition advice, and mandatory health screenings to help athletes prevent and recover from REDs.

gist: Celtic secured a seven to one victory against Hearts at Celtic Park.
Hearts suffered from severe defensive errors and psychological collapse during the match.
Celtic manager Martin O'Neill gained a much-needed win and praised his attacking players.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Celtic defeated Hearts seven to one in a match featuring early goals and multiple defensive mistakes by the visitors.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The emphatic win provides Celtic and manager Martin O'Neill with a significant boost after recent difficult periods.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Celtic aims to maintain this positive momentum over the long road ahead in the league campaign.

fivew: Martin O'Neill's Celtic team and Wouter Vrancken's Hearts team
Celtic defeated Hearts with a score of seven to one.
Hearts suffered from comically bad use of the ball and individual errors.
